Tools that call themselves language-agnostic codemod engines (often marketed as “polyglot” or “structural search-and-rewrite” frameworks) sit on top of parsers like Tree-sitter and give you one DSL to query / rewrite many languages. Besides OpenRewrite, the main players are:
*Engines inherit new languages whenever Tree-sitter (or an equivalent parser) adds one, so coverage keeps expanding.
Tree-sitter query + rewrite prototypes – experimental; you write a matcher and feed edits back to the tree. Good for bespoke tasks but no turnkey CLI. Tree-sitter
OpenRewrite – the widest JVM/ecosystem coverage plus YAML “recipes,” but outside JVM it only touches config formats (YAML/JSON/HCL). OpenRewrite Docs
CLI SSR built into IDEs – VS Code / IntelliJ structural replace; handy but not scriptable at repo scale. Tabnine
